original_question: For products of projective spaces (and, more generally, other interesting classes of varieties), classify special line bundles in the sense that there exists r ≥ 1 for which r generic double points fail to impose independent conditions on the line bundle.
target_in_paper: Section 1.1, Problem 2: "Classify special line bundles on the product of projective spaces. More generally, classify special line bundles on interesting classes of varieties," together with the immediately preceding definitions of "imposes independent conditions" and "special" as the Terracini-Lemma rephrasing of defective Segre-Veronese cases.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It identifies the correct ambient class (products of projective spaces), preserves the paper's deliberate broader add-on ("more generally" for interesting classes of varieties), and uses the right defining criterion for specialness: the existence of some r >= 1 for which generic double points fail to impose independent conditions.
missing_details: The paper gives a formal definition of "imposes independent conditions": for a zero-dimensional scheme Y ⊆ X, one requires dim H^0(I_Y ⊗ L) = max{dim H^0(L) - deg(Y), 0}.
The "r generic double points" should be described as a zero-dimensional scheme Y that is the union of r double points supported at general points of X.
The nearby notation states that the paper mainly works over the complex numbers.
The surrounding motivation is that, on products of projective spaces, this is the Terracini-Lemma reformulation of the defectivity question for Segre-Veronese embeddings.
To make the question stand alone, the ambient variety X and the zero-dimensional scheme Y ⊆ X should be notationally distinguished; the paper's nearby prose overloads X for both.
The paper does not specify any concrete broader class beyond saying "interesting classes of varieties," so a refined version should keep that phrase open rather than inserting new examples.
refined_question: Let X be a product of projective spaces over the complex numbers, and let L be a line bundle on X. Classify those line bundles L for which there exists an integer r >= 1 and a zero-dimensional scheme Y ⊆ X consisting of r double points supported at general points of X such that Y does not impose independent conditions on L, i.e. dim H^0(I_Y ⊗ L) != max{dim H^0(L) - deg(Y), 0}. More generally, ask the same classification for interesting classes of varieties.
equivalent_formulation: For X = P(V1) × ··· × P(Vk) and L = O_X(d1,...,dk), classify the tuples (n1,...,nk; d1,...,dk; r) for which the r-th secant variety of the Segre-Veronese embedding v_{d1,...,dk}(X) is defective; by Terracini's Lemma, this is equivalent to L being special in the sense above.
justification: The draft is targeting Section 1.1's Problem 2, not the broader neighboring Problem 1 or Problem 3. The match is exact at the level of keywords and quantifiers: the paper first defines when a zero-dimensional scheme imposes independent conditions on a line bundle, then defines a line bundle to be special when some number r of generic double points fail to do so, and immediately asks to classify such line bundles on products of projective spaces, with the same optional extension to other "interesting classes of varieties." The nearby context also explains that this viewpoint comes from Terracini's Lemma and the defectivity of Segre-Veronese secant varieties.
